text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me which part of your body hurts and how long you've been limping?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Since the pain is in the knee but there's no trauma, I need to check if the problem might actually be in the hip, as hip pain often refers to the knee in children. Can you tell me if he has any pain in his left hip or groin, and does the pain get worse at night or with activity?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Let me examine his hip movement to see if there is restricted internal rotation or pain on movement. I will also check for any swelling or tenderness in the knee itself to rule out local pathology.

text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: The patient is in the second grade, lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco or known toxins.

speaker: Doctor
text: I am now examining his hip range of motion. Does he experience pain or have limited movement when I try to internally rotate his left hip, or does the knee itself show signs of swelling and tenderness?
